summary: Tested the multi-tenant Pool Model (backend + UI). 21 pytest tests in /app/backend/tests/test_multitenant.py: 15 passed, 6 failed. Every failure is a real product bug, not a test problem. Things that work: the migration (all 29 operational collections are stamped demo-tenant-001/demo-branch-001, 0 unscoped docs, no unclassified collections); owner login with httpOnly SameSite=None cookies and bcrypt $2b$; /auth/me returns platform_role SUPERADMIN, tenant, active branch and branches; cookie-only auth works; brute-force lockout returns 429 on the 6th attempt. Tenant A cannot read, update or delete a demo client and demo cannot touch tenant A's (404, data unchanged). Tenant A sees empty lists/aggregations for 10 representative endpoints plus dashboard; demo WO/invoice by id return 404; creating a vehicle with a demo client_id returns 404. Quota: a 2nd branch over the limit returns 403 with the business message. Non-superadmin users (demo admin and tenant admin) get 403 on all /platform endpoints; unauthenticated calls get 401. Branch switching re-issues the token; data follows the branch strictly; switching to a branch that is not assigned, or belongs to another tenant, returns 403. Public quote reads only by token, hides the token, returns 404 for an invalid token, and rejects paper_approved=true with 403. Demo regression endpoints all return 200. UI: the panel is visible and works only for SUPERADMIN, demo admin sees the access-denied page and no nav link, the quota toast appears, and mobile 390px has no overflow (scrollWidth 390). Bugs found: global unique indexes and fixed singleton _id values give 500s and break tenant isolation; a TENANT_ADMIN can take over a SUPERADMIN account; document numbering (counters) is shared across tenants; cron background jobs crash with 'Context tenant lipsă'; the branch selector needs a reload after login, shows stale data after switching, and is hidden on mobile. All TEST data was removed, including main agent's leftover audit log from tenant-test-e1f6c296 and the work_order counter (restored to 98).

critical.issue: Privilege escalation. A TENANT_ADMIN (role admin) can reset the password of, or delete, any user in its tenant, including a platform_role=SUPERADMIN user. The test logged in with the new password and got 200 on /platform/tenants. In the demo tenant this means admin@serviceauto.ro can take over the owner andrei.melek. Fix: block updating/deleting users with platform_role unless the caller is SUPERADMIN.

Singleton docs use fixed _id values ('company', 'primary', 'main') in collections that are shared across tenants. The scoped upsert misses for a new tenant, then tries to insert the same _id and gets DuplicateKeyError (500). Result: new tenants cannot save company settings or e-Factura config. For RAR, only the first tenant to save can do it (tenant A got 200, tenant B got 500); demo has no RAR config yet, so any new tenant saving first would block demo. Fix: _id = f'{tenant}:{branch}:company' (or similar), or drop the fixed _id and use a unique index on (tenant_id, branch_id, kind).

Unique indexes are global: vehicles.vin, products.code, users.email. Tenant A registering a VIN that exists in demo gets 500 DuplicateKey, which also leaks that the VIN exists elsewhere. A product code collision behaves the same way (seen in code, not executed). POST /users only checks email uniqueness within the tenant, so an email used in another tenant gives a 500. Fix: make the indexes compound (tenant_id, branch_id, vin/code), or tenant-scoped as the business requires. For email: either keep global login uniqueness and check it globally (return 400), or redesign login.

Counters are global, so numbering for WO, invoices (SRV), NIR and payments is shared across tenants. Tenant A's first WO was CL-2026-00099, continuing demo's sequence. Romanian fiscal invoice series must be consecutive per issuer. Fix: scope counter keys per tenant/branch (e.g. _id=f'{tenant}:{branch}:invoice').

Background jobs run with no tenant scope, so TenantCollection raises HTTPException 503 'Context tenant lipsă'. Confirmed for reminders in backend.err.log ('Caught handled exception, but response already started'). e-Factura token refresh, status polling, inbox sync and reminders stop for every tenant while the endpoint still returns {ok:true}. Fix: loop over active tenants/branches and call set_scope for each, or use an explicit system_scope.

minor.issue: A cross-tenant update/delete changes nothing, but writes an audit log in the caller's tenant ('update client HACKED') before the 404 check. DELETE returns {ok:true} for an id that does not exist or belongs to another tenant. Fix: check existence first and return 404.

There is no API for SUPERADMIN to create the first TENANT_ADMIN of a new tenant, and none to assign several branches to a user. POST /users always assigns only the creator's active branch. The tests had to seed these users directly in the DB.

Methods without a wrapper (replace_one, find_one_and_delete, find_one_and_replace, bulk_write, estimated_document_count) fall through to the raw, unscoped collection. None are used today, but this is a silent bypass. Fix: raise for any method that is not wrapped. Also, $lookup inside aggregate pipelines is not scoped.
Takes a raw dict body, so a client could $set tenant_id/branch_id and move the settings doc to another tenant (mass assignment). Strip tenant_id/branch_id in _stamp/update, or validate with Pydantic.

ui_bugs.issue: The login response (user_out) has no 'branches' list, so a multi-branch user does not see the branch selector until the page is reloaded. Fix: call /auth/me after login, or include branches in the login response.

After switching branch, the current page keeps showing the previous branch's data (Clients list still showed the branch 1 client) until reload. The user may act on stale cross-branch records. Fix: reload the page or remount Outlet with key=active_branch_id after switching. switchBranch also has no try/catch or error toast.
The selector uses 'hidden md:block', so multi-branch users cannot switch branch on mobile (390px). Add it to the mobile Sheet or the header.

issues: No UI for PUT /platform/tenants/{id} (plan, quota, status) and no per-tenant branch list, although both APIs exist.
The 'Tenants activi' table lists every tenant, including SUSPENDED/EXPIRED ones; consider renaming it or filtering.

action_items: CRITICAL: Forbid a TENANT_ADMIN from updating or deleting users with platform_role (SUPERADMIN); only SUPERADMIN can manage them.
CRITICAL: Make singleton docs tenant-aware (settings 'company', rar_autopass_config 'primary', efactura_config 'main') to remove the 500 DuplicateKey.
HIGH: Change the global unique indexes vehicles.vin and products.code to compound tenant/branch indexes; turn the users.email collision into a 400 by checking globally.
HIGH: Scope counters per tenant/branch for WO, invoice, NIR, payment and proforma numbering.
HIGH: Make the cron jobs (e-Factura tokens/status/inbox, appointment reminders) loop over tenants/branches with set_scope.
HIGH (FE): Load branches after login; reload or remount the page after a branch switch; show the selector on mobile; handle switch errors.
MEDIUM: Add superadmin APIs to create the first TENANT_ADMIN of a tenant and to assign users to several branches.
MINOR: Check existence before audit on update/delete and return 404; make the TenantCollection fallback (__getattr__) refuse unwrapped methods; strip tenant_id/branch_id from raw dict updates.
critical_code_review_comments: core.TenantCollection.__getattr__ silently exposes the raw collection for methods without a wrapper, so the scope can be bypassed.
The aggregate scope adds a leading $match only; $lookup/$unionWith on other collections are unscoped.
write_settings $set uses the raw body dict, so tenant_id/branch_id can be overwritten.
server.startup calls set_scope(demo) for index creation; it is harmless because lifespan runs in its own task, but index creation should use raw_db explicitly.
routes_auth.login looks users up by email globally while POST /users checks uniqueness per tenant, which is inconsistent and gives 500s.
A migration that ran once still re-runs on every startup (idempotent, fine), but new collections are not validated against OPERATIONAL_COLLECTIONS; consider failing fast on unclassified collections.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_multitenant.py -n 1 -v (pytest.ini forces xdist). The fixture self-cleans tenants, users, operational data, audit logs and counters. The tests named test_vin_namespace_shared_across_tenants, test_settings_per_tenant, test_create_user_existing_email_other_tenant, test_tenant_admin_can_escalate..., test_shared_counter_numbering and test_rar_config_singleton_per_tenant assert the CORRECT behaviour and should pass once fixed. For the UI branch selector: python tests/mt_ui_fixture.py setup|cleanup (user test_ui_multi@example.com). Do not run the e-Factura cron against demo.
rca of the issue: Isolation is enforced by query filters only, but the DB constraints (unique indexes on _id, vin, code, email) and the counters are still global. Scoped upserts therefore miss for a new tenant and collide on insert, which gives the 500s, and numbering is shared. Escalation: update_user only checks that the target is in the same tenant and ignores platform_role. Cron: the scope comes from get_current_user, and cron requests have no user, so background tasks have no scope. FE: the login response lacks branches, and switchBranch does not invalidate page data.
